Regression guard for the prompt-coupling defect. The document is unmistakably a travel booking; only its dates are ambiguous. When the date-ambiguity rule was placed in the block shared by every capability, the classifier answered AMBIGUOUS 3/3 - the extractor's question, answered by the wrong capability, which suppressed extraction entirely. AMBIGUOUS is a FAILURE here.
Injected instructions must not alter the category. Correct 3/3 in the M8 spike.

UNSUPPORTED is the pass. This is UKVI correspondence about indefinite leave to remain and it confirms no grant of anything - IMMIGRATION_STATUS is for correspondence 'confirming a grant of status', and an acknowledgement confirms receipt. Deliberately not one of the prompt's own UNSUPPORTED examples (bank statement, payslip, tenancy agreement), which would test whether the model can read its instructions back. `document_type` is IMMIGRATION_STATUS on purpose: it is what a user filing this would choose, and the classifier disagreeing with the uploader out loud is the behaviour M8 slice 2 built. The failure has teeth - called IMMIGRATION_STATUS, this goes to an extractor hunting a grant date it does not contain, and the nearest date on the page is the day it was received.

AMBIGUOUS is the pass, and it is ambiguous between two *supported* categories - which is what the category means, as against UNSUPPORTED meaning none of them. A test-centre pass notification is either an English language result or a Life in the UK result and nothing on it says which. Both have real extractors, so forcing a choice sends the document to one of two schemas on a coin toss. Sparse rather than damaged: perfectly legible and still undetermined. No must_not_extract - the expectation already fails on any real category, and a redundant forbidden list risks firing on a reasoning field that names the two candidates, which is exactly what an honest AMBIGUOUS answer would do.

Held out from the prompt that was written to fix this class of failure. classify_document.v2 gives IMMIGRATION_STATUS the condition 'states that leave or status HAS BEEN GRANTED' and lists the non-grants it excludes: acknowledges, requests documents, confirms a fee, schedules an appointment, defers, refuses. A withdrawal at the applicant's request is on none of that list and is still not a grant, so this fixture measures whether v2 taught a principle or an example. Deliberately not a refusal - v2 names refusals, and a fixture drawn from the list would only check whether the model can read the list back. If this passes while the acknowledgement fixture passes, the condition generalises at least once; if it fails while that one passes, v2 is overfitted and the measurement says so.
